evidence_ledger.rationale: The paragraph index exposes 1000-MAIN, 2000-DUE-DATE, and 3000-COMPARE, establishing the implementation path to inspect.
1000-MAIN performs both due-date calculation and comparison before displaying escalation, so the regulated action is present rather than absent.
The entry paragraph invokes 2000-DUE-DATE and 3000-COMPARE, establishing reachability of the compliance path.
2000-DUE-DATE copies the complaint day and advances the month by one, with December rollover; this constructs a calendar-month interval that can exceed 30 days.
The source comparator is the exact token > and its true branch sets escalation; this is not token-only D5 evidence, because the preceding due-date computation determines the elapsed interval.
The inspected data layout is a typed YYYY/MM/DD complaint date, not an enum_set reference collection, so D4 is inapplicable.
The check date is also a typed YYYY/MM/DD structure, confirming that the comparison evaluates date behavior.
A scoped grep for 30 finds only the paragraph name and PERFORM reference; there is no 30-day literal threshold to support a D1 stale-value claim.
WS-DUE-DATE is used by the IF at line 42 in 3000-COMPARE, linking the computed calendar-month date to the escalation decision.
The trace records live definitions MOVE 01 TO WS-DUE-MM and COMPUTE WS-DUE-MM = WS-CMP-MM + 1 in 2000-DUE-DATE.
The WS-DUE-MM slice includes the complaint month, December branch, January reset, and +1 month computation in the reachable intraprocedural due-date paragraph.
The WS-DUE-DD slice shows WS-CMP-DD copied directly to WS-DUE-DD, completing a calendar-month due-date construction rather than a fixed day-count addition.
The WS-DUE-YYYY slice shows December year increment and unchanged non-December year, confirming complete calendar-month arithmetic.
WS-ESCALATE has a default N, a display use, and a reachable MOVE Y in 3000-COMPARE, so the compliance action is not dead.
A one-calendar-month due date is not positive evidence matching the clause's fixed maximum of 30 days, so D7 conformance is not met.

response.thought: The reachable implementation computes the due date one calendar month after lodging and then escalates after that computed date. Because calendar months can exceed 30 days, this is a positive contradiction of the maximum-30-day clause.

prediction.rationale: GRVAGE1 copies the complaint day, advances the complaint month by one with December rollover, and uses that calendar-month date as WS-DUE-DATE. 3000-COMPARE then tests WS-CHECK-DATE > WS-DUE-DATE and moves Y to WS-ESCALATE. Since a calendar month can be 31 days, the reachable behavior can permit more than the clause's maximum 30 days; the contradiction is caused by the due-date computation, not by a comparator-only boundary token.

response.claim: If a complainant does not get a satisfactory response within a maximum period of 30 days from lodging the complaint, they may approach the RBI Ombudsman.
response.final_answer: GRVAGE1 computes the due date one calendar month after the complaint date and escalates only when the check date is later than that date, which can allow more than the clause's maximum 30 days.
